messages.subject: How to run multiple unmarked models in parallel?
parts:
Dear friends,

There has been some discussion about using parallel processing to reduce the time required to use parboot() to evaluate goodness-of-fit of a particular unmarked model. For example, here are two threads providing good solutions:

https://groups.google.com/forum/#!msg/unmarked/txp1UeptjgM/bYHTPiUN55kJ


https://groups.google.com/forum/#!searchin/unmarked/parallel$20parboot$20%7Csort:date/unmarked/9vXaxj-7chU/jfgX4WEKBAAJ



Now, I'd like to use parallel processing to run reduce the time required to fit dozens of gmultmix() models on large datasets. Each of my ~50 models takes ~30 minutes to fit, and I'd like to fit all of the models for ~6 species or guilds, so fitting these one at a time would take several weeks. Thus, my desire to use parallel processing (on a cloud-based machine with 96 cores).


The parboot() examples linked above involve doing the same thing (a parboot call) many times, but this current problem involves doing many things (fit different models) once each. I can't find any coded examples of using parallel processing to fit multiple models in parallel either in the this Google group or elsewhere (stackoverflow etc), so I'm hoping someone here might be able to point me in the right direction.


Many thanks in advance!


Mark B.

messages.subject: Re: How to run multiple unmarked models in parallel?
parts:
Hi Mark,

Here's a rough example that should get you started.

Also, the pre-release version of unmarked on Github has a new C++ backend for gmultmix. In my tests the new backend is 10-15 times faster than the old pure-R version, but it only supports the built in pi functions (removal, double).

#run 2 models in parallel
library(unmarked)
library(parallel)


data(frogs)
pferUMF <- unmarkedFrameOccu(pfer.bin)


#Add second dataset
pferUMF2 <- pferUMF
siteCovs(pferUMF2) <- data.frame(sitevar1 = rnorm(numSites(pferUMF2)))
obsCovs(pferUMF2) <- data.frame(obsvar1 = rnorm(numSites(pferUMF2) * obsNum(pferUMF2)))


#Set up parallel
nmods <- 2
processors <- detectCores() - 1
cl <- makeCluster(processors)


#function to run unmarked in each core
#could add more arguments to call
run_um <- function(x){
  unmarked::occu(as.formula(x[[1]]),x[[2]])
}


#Sets of arguments for each run (list of lists)
#Could add more arguments here
args <- list(mod1=list(formula='~1 ~1', data=pferUMF),
             mod2=list(formula='~obsvar1 ~1', data=pferUMF2))


#Run in parallel
out <- parLapply(cl=cl,X=args,fun=run_um)


stopCluster(cl)
#Result is list with each element being one model output

Hi Ken,

Thanks again for this example code. I got it working yesterday and at this point I have one main question. You have to provide each argument to gmultmix in a separate element of each list. In my original example I had only 'formula' and 'data' arguments because that's all occu() needs, but gmultmix needs three separate formulas and potentially the mixture argument.

I wrote out a (shortened) version of your code that hopefully will be more clear (note I didn't actually run this, but it should work):

library(unmarked)
library(parallel)

processors <- detectCores() - 1
cl <- makeCluster(processors)

# define function to run unmarked in each core
run_um <- function(x){

#assume mixture is poisson unless specified explicitly
  #if you specify the mixture in every list of arguments below you can remove this part
  if(is.null(x$mixture)){
    x$mixture <- "P"
  }


  unmarked::gmultmix(lambdaformula=as.formula(x$lambdaformula),
                      phiformula=as.formula(x$phiformula),
                      pformula=as.formula(x$pformula),
                      mixture=x$mixture,
                      data=x$data)

}


# Sets of arguments for each run (list of lists)

#Each formula and the mixture argument should be their own list element
#I cut out some models just to save typing
args <- list(fm0=list(lambdaformula='~1', phiformula= '~1', pformula='~1', data=ovenFrame),
              fm1 = list(lambdaformula='~ ufc', phiformula='~ 1', pformula='~ 1', data = ovenFrame),
              fm1nb = list(lambdaformula='~ ufc', phiformula='~ 1', pformula='~ 1', mixture = "NB", data = ovenFrame),

You have to provide each argument to gmultmix in a separate element of each list. In my original example I had only 'formula' and 'data' arguments because that's all occu() needs, but gmultmix needs three separate formulas and potentially the mixture argument.

library(unmarked)
library(parallel)


processors <- detectCores() - 1
cl <- makeCluster(processors)


# define function to run unmarked in each core
run_um <- function(x){
  #assume mixture is poisson unless specified explicitly
  #if you specify the mixture in every list of arguments below you can remove this part
  if(is.null(x$mixture)){
    x$mixture <- "P"
  }


  unmarked::gmultmix(lambdaformula=as.formula(x$lambdaformula),
                      phiformula=as.formula(x$phiformula),
                      pformula=as.formula(x$pformula),
                      mixture=x$mixture,
                      data=x$data)


}


# Sets of arguments for each run (list of lists)
